paper_metadata.title: Tensile properties and fracture toughness of TiAl alloys with controlled microstructures

evidence.quote: The objective of this study is to improve the mechanical properties by careful control of both microstructure and alloy additions in two-phase TiAl alloys based on Ti-47Al-2Cr-2Nb (at%).

Our studies show that the mechanical properties of the TIA alloys with lamellar structures are dependent on three interrelated factors: (1) colony size, (2) interlamellar spacings, and (3) alloy addi- tion.

mechanisms.name: lamellar colony size effect on ductility

evidence.quote: The tensile elongation at room temperature is strongly dependent on lamellar colony size, showing increasing ductility with decreased colony size.
The strength at room and elevated temperatures is sensitive to interlamellar spacing, showing increasing strength with decreased colony spacing.
This delamination absorbs energy and significantly contributes to the increase in the fracture toughness caused by heat-treating at 1320°C as opposed to 900°C (see Fig. 11).
The increase in the strength with decreasing lamel- lar spacing is consistent with the prediction from a Hall-Petoh relationship which is generally found to be applicable to two-phase TiAl alloys.
The beneficial effect of tungsten may come from the refinement of lamel- lar structure observed by TEM.

conflicts.description: The same original sample designation TIA-20 is assigned two different compositions across segments: Ti-47Al-2Cr-2Nb-0.15B (Table 1, part 001) versus Ti47Al-2Cr-2Nb-0.2W (part 002). The part 002 mapping appears to be an erroneous alias derived from prose about tungsten-bearing alloys; both are preserved unmerged.
